doc.title: Sam Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Future of jazz students and work
summary: Whether young jazz players will find places to practice and work.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: It comes around now that you can buy it to practice along with it.
Well there’s so much available these days. What’s going to happen with the wealth of jazz students? Do you think they’ll have a place to practice their craft in the future?

Yeah, I’m not sure whether there’s going to be enough work although they say the cream will rise to the top if there’s some outstanding musicians I guess somebody’ll say this guy’s too good like to — you know, you have to discover them.

I guess so but I don’t know what’s going to happen to all those people, either stage band people or people that play with the bands. I understand there’s a lot of good people coming out, that some bands hire people from here and there, North Texas State or Berklee.
